The updated guidelines provide recommendations on first-line and second-line antiretroviral (ARV) regimens, post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), and early infant diagnosis of HIV. These guidelines supplement the 2016 consolidated guidelines on the use of ARV drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection. The recommendations were developed following WHO standards for guideline development, based on systematic reviews of evidence, and supplemented with additional information on values, preferences, feasibility, and acceptability. In 2016, WHO recommended an efavirenz (EFV 600 mg)-based regimen as the preferred first-line option, with dolutegravir (DTG)or efavirenz (400 mg)-based regimens as alternatives due to limited efficacy and safety data in pregnancy and during tuberculosis (TB) co-treatment. ART recommendations for children remained unchanged due to the lack of approved DTG dosing for pediatric use. Since then, evidence has accumulated on the use of DTG in firstand second-line ART, including during pregnancy, TB co-treatment, and for children. The updated guidelines now include recommendations for these populations and updated guidance on ARV drugs for HIV PEP. Additionally, a new recommendation is provided for interpreting early infant diagnosis test results to improve diagnostic accuracy.
